title: Network Pharmacology and Molecular Docking Combined with In Vivo Validation to Elucidate the Molecular Mechanisms of Adenophorae Radix in Fracture Healing.
authors: Park, Jiin; Kim, Jin Hee; Huh, Eugene; Lee, Minji; Lee, Seungmin; Youn, Yousuk; Lee, Sangho; Oh, Myung Sook
one_liner_zh: 该文用网络药理学和分子对接研究中药沙参促进骨折愈合的机制，虽含分子对接但对象为化合物-蛋白，非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Fracture healing is a multistage regenerative process requiring the coordinated regulation of inflammation, osteogenesis, and bone remodeling, yet pharmacological agents that effectively modulate these processes remain limited. Adenophorae Radix (AR), a traditional medicinal herb used for tissue repair, has not been mechanistically investigated in skeletal regeneration. In this study, a mouse femoral fracture model was employed to evaluate the effects of short-term (7 days) and long-term (5 weeks) oral administration of AR. Bone regeneration was assessed using micro-computed tomography, histological staining, and quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction. Network pharmacology and molecular docking were applied to predict bioactive AR constituents and their target pathways, followed by in vivo validation. Short-term AR treatment significantly upregulated osteogenic markers, including RUNX2 and osteocalcin, in the bone marrow, indicating early activation of osteoblast differentiation. Long-term administration enhanced bone mineral density, trabecular organization, and callus maturation. Network pharmacology analysis identified cycloartenol acetate, beta-sitosterol, and mandenol as major active compounds targeting osteogenesis- and osteoclast-related pathways, converging on HIF1A, PTGS2, and PPARG. Molecular docking demonstrated strong binding affinities between these compounds and their predicted targets, which was supported by increased expression of HIF1A, PTGS2, and PPARG in AR-treated femora. Collectively, these findings suggest that AR promotes fracture healing by regulating osteogenic differentiation and bone remodeling through multi-target transcriptional networks.
abstract_zh: 骨折愈合是一个多阶段的再生过程，需要炎症、成骨和骨重塑的协调调控，然而能有效调节这些过程的药物仍然有限。轮叶党参（Adenophorae Radix, AR）是一种用于组织修复的传统草药，但其在骨骼再生中的机制尚未被研究。本研究采用小鼠股骨骨折模型，评估短期（7天）和长期（5周）口服AR的效果。通过微型计算机断层扫描、组织学染色和定量实时聚合酶链反应评估骨再生。应用网络药理学和分子对接预测AR的生物活性成分及其靶向通路，随后进行体内验证。短期AR治疗显著上调骨髓中成骨标志物，包括RUNX2和骨钙素，表明成骨细胞分化的早期激活。长期给药增强了骨矿物质密度、骨小梁组织和骨痂成熟。网络药理学分析鉴定出环阿屯醇乙酸酯、β-谷甾醇和甘露醇为主要活性化合物，靶向成骨和破骨相关通路，汇聚于HIF1A、PTGS2和PPARG。分子对接显示这些化合物与其预测靶点之间具有强结合亲和力，这得到了AR处理股骨中HIF1A、PTGS2和PPARG表达增加的证实。总体而言，这些发现表明AR通过多靶点转录网络调节成骨分化和骨重塑，从而促进骨折愈合。
